x: We have yet to win the team race in this classic race, and this year it seemed even less likely that we should do so, for we were without the assistance of Colin Collis, Eric Gebbett and Bob Plummer.
Chas Walker was placed third in the Civil Service 5 miles cross-country championship and Dave Baulch was eighth. Bob Plummer, now recovered from his knee trouble plans a full season for 1958.
Bob Plummer, better known for his exploits over the marathon distance, took advantage of the handicapper's generosity to win the handicap by a good margin.
Bob Plummer,by gaining 11th place,completed our scoring team which was beaten by T.V.H. by the narrow margin of two points. All our six starters completed the course - quite a good effort.

On a rather warm day, and in a field of close on one hundred starters, Eric Gebbett performed very well to finish in 8th place with a time of 1h.25m.18s. He was well backed up by Eric Bishop in 13th place and Bob Plummer 16th. In the team race we just pipped Mitcham for third place.

The third Club runner to finish was Bob Plummer, who recorded his best ever time of 2h.36m.46s. to occupy 25th position. Bob has now regained the excellent form he was showing two years ago when he was laid low by a very troublesome knee injury.
With Bob Plummer running well for twelfth place our team was narrowly beaten by T.V.H. Mention must be made of Ron Linstead and Joe Dooley, who were running in their first 20 mile race.
At five miles our four, Alan Bishop, Joe MacDonald, Bob Plummer and Wally Wortley were running together at just inside seven minutes a mile.
Walker were well to the fore early on, and with Colin Collis, Archie Bedford, Len Bishop and Bob Plummer quite well placed, it seemed as if we might gain a team place in this well contested race.

With such a fast winning time many meritorious performances "down the field" are apt to be overlooked, but Colin Collis deserves special mention for his 11th place in 1h.50m.50s as does Bob Plummer for his best ever time of 1h.52m.54s.

Then came Len Bishop in 3rd. place Eric 9th, Bob Glover (coerced into running by Ken Stimpson) 10th!, with Alan Bishop, Joe Dooley and Bob Plummer running well together in 14th position - 1 min.49 secs. down on the leaders.

Arthur and his road running group (now comprising Denis Brickwood, Geoff Pearson, George Chantler, Wally Wortly, Arthur Penstone, Bob Plummer and Joe MacDonald among others) ran all these races over the next few years.
